sources.title: John Higham, “Changing Paradigms: The Collapse of Consensus History” (1989).
sources.citation: John Higham, “Changing Paradigms: The Collapse of Consensus History,” Journal of American History76,no.2(September1989),460–466; archived Charles University teaching scan at https://web.archive.org/web/20160303232146id_/http://tucnak.fsv.cuni.cz/~calda/Higham_Paradigms_ConsensusHistory.pdf.

verification.note: Fresh archived JSTOR scan retrieved200. All printed460–466 and notes1–10 freshly read through local OCR; printed460–462 and464 visually collated. Eight PDF pages comprise cover plus seven article pages. Higham’s1989 judgment that consensus writers never formed a school qualifies his own earlier naming. Thomas Kuhn explicitly credited but paradigm is expressly a looser shorthand. The E.P.Thompson quotation is named in body462 although note4 cites Tocqueville rather than identifying a Thompson work; no missing reference is invented. Tyrrell’s account is named mediation for the advanced1960s Marxist scholarship judgment. Underlying cited works,1968 lecture and full1983 History edition unread; no independent certification of every reception/general historical assertion.
